newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-MILAN FACE FURTHER PROBLEMS AGAINST VICENZA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MILAN FACE FURTHER PROBLEMS AGAINST VICENZA.

text.p: Out-of-form Italian soccer champions AC Milan may be in for another uncomfortable game on Sunday, at home to second-placed Vicenza.
Milan, already eliminated from both the Champions' League and the Italian Cup, have lost six out of 15 league games this season to drop to ninth place in the table.
A 3-0 away defeat by Lazio last Sunday probably represented a low point in a miserable season for a side accustomed to dominating Italian and European soccer.
Coach Arrigo Sacchi, who was brought in to replace Uruguyan Oscar Washington Tabarez in early December, believes his side needs a radical overhaul, telling reporters in midweek :
"Some of my players bear no blame for the way things have gone, others a great deal of blame...In five months, this team has lost 10 games, almost 50 per cent of its matches.
"Obviously, if you lose that often then the problems are serious and if we can find a way out of this (crisis) at all it will certainly not be a short term way out."
First step in the Sacchi overhaul was the midweek sale of Milan's Italian international defender Christian Panucci to Spanish league leaders Real Madrid for a reported $5.3 million dollars.
Furthermore Sacchi is allegedly unhappy with the form of playmaker Roberto Baggio and central defender Alessandro Costacurta and both may be dropped against Vicenza on Sunday.
Sacchi will also be without four injured players -- Liberian striker George Weah, French striker Christophe Dugarry and defenders Paolo Maldini and Pietro Vierchowod.
Frenchman Marcel Desailly drops back from midfield to replace Costacurta in defence while Marco Simone teams up with Yugoslav Dejan Savicevic in attack.
Sacchi is also likely to field two 19-year-olds in midfielder Massimo Ambrosini and defender Francesco Coco.
In-form Vicenza, the side who eliminated Milan from the Italian Cup in November, come into the game on 26 points, just three behind leaders Juventus and five clear of Milan.
Vicenza should be at close to full strength with only their Uruguyan defender Gustavo Mendez unavailable because of World Cup duty.
Roberto Murgita leads the attack with Uruguyan striker Marcelo Otero playing behind him, while Fabio Viviani and Domenico Di Carlo play in their accustomed central midfield roles.
